newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel backs down on budget cuts, higher taxes seen.
newsitem.headline: Israel backs down on budget cuts, higher taxes seen.

text.p: Israel's treasury, caving in to demands to slash a range of social services and turning to tax hikes on cigarettes and petrol to boost revenues, has narrowly cleared a parliamentary hurdle to approval of its 1997 budget.
Parliament's finance committee voted late on Sunday to approve a package of revamped proposals aimed at trimming the budget, lawmakers said on Monday.

Key members of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's ruling Likud party had demanded that cuts in social services be softened as a condition for their support when the budget is brought before parliament for approval by year's end.
The treasury failed to gain approval of any of its proposals on health issues, among them increases in patient fees for physican services and in the price of drugs.
Also nullified were proposed cuts in grants to parents of small children and to former soldiers who have recently completed service in combat units.
Stiff hikes are expected in taxes on cigarettes and petrol to offset the cancelled budget cut proposals, parliamentary sources said.
The levies, something of an embarassment to the government which had pledged to refrain from new taxes, are to be announced in the coming days, they said.
